# API Rate Limiting Per Tenant

## Problem

The current rate limiter applies a single global threshold across all tenants, causing high-traffic tenants to degrade service for others sharing the same tier.

## Goal

Implement per-tenant rate limiting so that each tenant's quota is enforced independently, preventing noisy-neighbour effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each tenant has a configurable requests-per-minute quota stored in the tenants table
- [ ] The rate limiter reads the per-tenant quota on each request and enforces it independently
- [ ] Requests exceeding the tenant quota return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header
- [ ] Quota changes take effect within 60 seconds without a service restart
- [ ] Rate limit metrics are emitted per tenant to the existing Prometheus endpoint

## Approach

Extend the existing `RateLimiter` middleware to look up tenant config from a Redis-backed cache (TTL 60 s). Fallback to the global default if no tenant-specific quota is found.

## Codebase Context

The rate limiter lives in `middleware/rate_limit.go`. Tenant config is currently stored in Postgres `tenants` table with no Redis cache layer.

# Fix Tooltip Overflow on Narrow Viewports

## Problem

Chart tooltips overflow the viewport edge on screens narrower than 768 px, obscuring data and breaking the layout on mobile browsers.

## Goal

Ensure tooltips reposition themselves to stay fully within the viewport on all screen widths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tooltip stays fully visible on viewports as narrow as 320 px
- [ ] Repositioning animation completes in under 150 ms
- [ ] No regression in tooltip behaviour on desktop (>= 1280 px)

## Approach

Update `TooltipPortal` component to calculate available space on mount and flip placement when the tooltip would overflow. Use `getBoundingClientRect` rather than fixed pixel offsets.

## Risks

Calculating bounding rects on every render may introduce jank on low-end devices; gate the recalculation behind `requestAnimationFrame` to keep the main thread unblocked.

# Push Notification Preference Centre

## Problem

Users have no granular control over which push notifications they receive, leading to high unsubscribe rates and app uninstalls driven by notification fatigue.

## Goal

Deliver an in-app preference centre where users can toggle notification categories independently on iOS and Android.

## User Stories

- As a user I want to disable marketing notifications without turning off transactional alerts.
- As a user I want my preferences to sync across devices instantly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Preference centre screen is accessible from Settings > Notifications
- [ ] Users can toggle at least six notification categories independently
- [ ] Toggling a category takes effect within 5 seconds on the device
- [ ] Preferences are persisted server-side and synced across all logged-in devices
- [ ] A user who disables all categories sees a confirmation prompt before saving
- [ ] Deep-link `prdx://settings/notifications` opens the preference centre directly
- [ ] Analytics event `notification_pref_changed` is fired on every toggle

## Approach

Build a `NotificationPreferencesScreen` in React Native. Sync state via a new `PATCH /users/{id}/notification-preferences` endpoint. Store preferences in the existing user-profile service.

## Risks

- FCM/APNs quota limits may delay preference propagation; show a "changes saved" toast immediately and reconcile asynchronously.
- iOS 17 permission prompt changes may affect how category toggles interact with system-level settings.

## Open Questions

- Should we allow per-device overrides in addition to account-wide preferences?
- Do we need a digest / batching mode for high-frequency categories?

# Consolidate CI Build Stages

## Problem

The CI pipeline has grown to 14 separate stages, many of which run sequentially despite having no dependency on each other, inflating median build time to 22 minutes.

## Goal

Reduce median CI build time to under 10 minutes by parallelising independent stages and removing redundant steps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Lint, unit tests, and type-check jobs run in parallel in a single workflow stage
- [ ] Docker image build is cached between runs using layer caching on the registry
- [ ] End-to-end tests run only on changes to `src/` or `e2e/` paths
- [ ] Median build time on the main branch drops below 10 minutes within two weeks of rollout
- [ ] No currently passing test suite is dropped or skipped

## Approach

Refactor `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to use job-level parallelism. Add `paths` filters to the E2E job. Enable GitHub Actions cache for Docker layers with a per-branch cache key.

# Evaluate Feature Store Solutions: Feast vs Tecton

## Problem

The data science team is computing the same feature transformations independently in training pipelines and the inference service, causing training-serving skew and duplicated engineering effort.

## Goal

Produce a short technical report comparing Feast and Tecton on cost, operational overhead, and compatibility with our existing Spark + BigQuery stack.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Evaluation covers latency, cost, and operational burden for both tools
- [ ] A working proof-of-concept is built for the top candidate using at least two existing features
- [ ] Report and PoC artefacts are committed to `docs/spikes/feature-store/`

## Approach

Run a two-week timebox: week 1 sets up both tools locally and benchmarks feature retrieval latency; week 2 builds the PoC for the winner and writes up findings.

## Open Questions

- Are there licensing or data-residency constraints that would rule out Tecton for our EU tenants?
- Can Feast handle our current feature-serving SLA of < 20 ms p99?

# Webhook Delivery: Exponential Backoff Retry

## Problem

Failed webhook deliveries are retried at a fixed 30-second interval, causing thundering-herd behaviour against slow or recovering subscriber endpoints.

## Goal

Replace fixed-interval retries with exponential backoff (base 2, max 1 hour) with jitter, as a child item of the broader webhook reliability epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Retry schedule uses exponential backoff: 30 s, 1 min, 2 min, 4 min up to 1 h
- [ ] Each retry interval includes +/- 10% random jitter
- [ ] After 24 hours of consecutive failures the webhook subscription is marked `suspended`
- [ ] Suspended subscriptions emit a `webhook.suspended` event to the audit log
- [ ] Operators can manually re-enable a suspended subscription via the admin API
- [ ] Retry schedule is visible in the existing webhook delivery log UI
- [ ] Unit tests cover boundary conditions: first retry, max-interval cap, suspension threshold

## Approach

Extend `WebhookDispatcher` with a `BackoffScheduler` component. Store next-retry timestamps in the `webhook_deliveries` table. Add a background job that polls for due retries every 10 seconds.

# Migrate Legacy Button Components to Design System v3

## Problem

The codebase contains three separate button implementations (`LegacyButton`, `OldPrimaryButton`, `ActionBtn`) that diverge from the Design System v3 spec, causing visual inconsistency and duplicated accessibility fixes across teams.

## Goal

Replace all usages of the three legacy button components with the canonical `Button` component from `@acme/design-system-v3`, deleting the legacy source files.

## User Stories

- As a developer I want a single `Button` import so I don't have to decide which legacy variant to use.
- As a designer I want consistent button rendering across the app so mockups match production exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All `LegacyButton`, `OldPrimaryButton`, and `ActionBtn` usages are replaced with `Button` from v3
- [ ] Legacy source files and their unit tests are deleted
- [ ] Visual regression tests pass with no diff on Chromatic
- [ ] Bundle size does not increase by more than 1 kB after the migration
- [ ] Accessibility audit (axe-core) reports no new violations

## Approach

Use an AST codemod (`jscodeshift`) to automate the bulk of the migration, then manually review edge cases flagged by the codemod. Run Chromatic and axe-core in CI as required gates before merging.

# Fix Crash When Biometric Auth Falls Back to PIN

## Problem

On Android 12 devices, the app crashes with a `NullPointerException` in `BiometricManager` when the user cancels Face Unlock and the system falls back to PIN entry.

## Goal

Handle the biometric-to-PIN fallback gracefully without crashing, keeping the user in the authentication flow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cancelling Face Unlock on Android 12 falls back to PIN prompt without crashing
- [ ] The error is logged to Crashlytics with the device model and Android version
- [ ] Existing biometric auth tests pass on Android 11, 13, and 14

## Approach

Wrap the `BiometricPrompt.AuthenticationCallback.onAuthenticationError` handler in a null check before accessing `biometricResult`. Add a targeted automated test using Espresso's `BiometricTestRule` to reproduce the Android 12 fallback scenario in CI.

# Incremental dbt Model Refresh

## Problem

Full-refresh dbt runs against the events table take 45+ minutes, blocking the daily dashboard refresh and making ad-hoc re-runs prohibitively expensive for the analytics team.

## Goal

Convert the five highest-cost dbt models to incremental materialisation so routine runs process only new rows, as part of the dbt performance epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The five target models use `incremental` materialisation with a documented `unique_key`
- [ ] Incremental run duration is under 5 minutes for a standard daily delta
- [ ] A full-refresh flag remains available for schema migrations
- [ ] Data quality tests (`dbt test`) pass after both incremental and full-refresh runs
- [ ] Incremental logic is documented in each model's `.yml` description

## Approach

Add `{{ config(materialized='incremental', unique_key='event_id') }}` blocks to each model. Use the `is_incremental()` macro to filter to new rows. Validate with a shadow run in the staging environment before promoting to production.

# Vault Dynamic Secret Rotation

## Probelm

Hardcoded database credentials in environment variables are rotated manually every 90 days, creating a risk window and significant operational toil for the platform team.

## Goal

Use HashiCorp Vault's dynamic secrets engine to issue short-lived database credentials automatically, eliminating static secrets from the environment entirely.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Vault dynamic secrets are enabled for the primary Postgres instance
2. App pods fetch a fresh credential on startup via the Vault agent sidecar
3. Credential TTL is set to 1 hour with a max TTL of 4 hours
4. Rotation does not cause connection drops; the connection pool is re-initialised on lease renewal
5. Audit log captures every credential issuance and revocation event

## Approch

Deploy the Vault agent sidecar via the existing Helm chart. Configure the `database` secrets engine with a role bound to the app service account. Update app startup scripts to source credentials from the Vault agent socket.

## Codebase Context

Vault is already deployed in the cluster at `vault.internal`. The Helm chart lives at `infra/helm/vault-agent/`.
